abstract: Communities in the United States and around the world are contesting data centers, the physical infrastructure of AI. These disputes pose environmental justice issues: residents must weigh unevenly distributed burdens using evidence scattered across metrics, corporate claims, policy documents, and public testimony. A formative study with 10 users showed that dashboards and single-agent AI can settle questions before people examine that evidence. Here we present EJAI, a source-grounded system that links an interactive map, retrieved evidence, missing-data statements, and two stakeholder personas that allow people to inspect evidence and form their own policy recommendations. In a small functional benchmark of 21 queries, retrieved evidence supported 98.4% of factual claims and the system acknowledged missing evidence in 32 of 33 cases. Persona alignment carried a grounding cost: the Corporate Executive omitted some evidence that conflicted with its assigned priorities. In a within-subjects study, 15 participants acting as residents prepared for a simulated town hall. Some checked cited AI claims while treating map metrics as official, some made conditional recommendations with safeguards such as water-use disclosure, and some found the personas simplified or biased. Our results suggest that civic AI can support preparation for public reasoning when it makes evidence, gaps, and disagreement open to inspection, and that corpus imbalance and two-sided personas remain open justice concerns.

ur.tldr: EJAI通过交互地图、检索证据、缺失数据说明及利益相关者角色，帮助居民自行形成数据中心环境政策建议。21项查询中98.4%的事实主张获证据支持，33项缺证情形中32项被承认；但角色立场可能遗漏冲突证据，说明来源可追溯与分歧可见性是保障独立判断的关键。

title: EJAI: Judgment-Preserving Civic AI for Data Center Environmental Justice
title_zh: EJAI：面向数据中心环境正义的判断保全型公民AI
